description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Gitleaks fixture that carries one record whose rule identifier is present but empty. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Key names follow expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, the first negative expected file in this folder: every key the positive sibling expected/gitleaks.rows.json uses is reused here with the same meaning, and the negative-only structures -- routing, rejection_boundary, rejections and counts.parse_status -- are additive, so one generic loader reads them all.
scanner_class_note: Fixed per tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and authored as a constant in the adapter (SCANNER_CLASS). Trivy is the single tool whose class varies per record; this one never does, so no row below takes its class from record content -- and the rejected record does not take one at all, because it produces no row.
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the whole document; AAP 0.7 says the same. No rule is cited or invented here, and none forces this file into scope -- it exists because AAP 0.6.1 pairs every negative fixture with a hand-verified expected file, AAP 0.6.2 requires one negative fixture per rejection condition each exercised adapter can produce, and AAP 0.9.4 makes those assertions part of the definition of done. The absence of rules is not licence to lower the bar: every value below is hand-verified from the fixture rather than recorded from a run.

fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Three of the four elements are byte-identical to elements of the declared-derived oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json -- /0 to its /1, /2 to its /3 and /3 to its /2 -- compared field by field including key order. The fourth, /1, is the synthesized defective record: it is element /2 with its RuleID emptied to the empty string, and the two differ in exactly two keys, RuleID and Fingerprint.
fixture.captured_provenance: No element here equals the raw artifact's sole record: harness/artifacts/raw/gitleaks.json holds exactly one finding, this provisioning's single leak in python/pyspark/pandas/groupby.py, and it is not among these four. Every element is therefore derived, in the tool's own eighteen-key shape and key order, which oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json states of the five it derived. The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these values are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- routing is keyed by the writing runner, never sniffed from content. is_sarif(doc) is false for this document: it carries neither a version of '2.1.0' nor a runs array, being a bare array of finding objects.
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route('gitleaks', doc) returns tool 'gitleaks', shape 'native', adapter 'gitleaks', scanner_class 'secret'
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is the bare array this shape requires and routes cleanly; exactly one record inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that record while still emitting the others.
routing.not_the_adapter_error_either: Nor is a GitleaksAdapterError expected. That exception describes a defective call -- the wrong tool identifier, a relative root, another tool's path base, or a document whose top level is not a JSON array -- and stops the caller. A defective record inside a well-formed array is counted, not raised.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. This document is a native artifact and would serve that assertion, but it is not this file's job to make it.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

reference_behaviours.behaviour: the missing_rule_id rejection in its empty-string form
reference_behaviours.what_this_file_fixes: One counted rejection under missing_rule_id for element /1, whose RuleID is present as the empty string, with the three well-formed elements still emitted as rows.
reference_behaviours.why_it_belongs_here: This is the folder's reference assertion that an identifier which is present but carries no value is an absence rather than a value. A test that only counted rejections could not tell this condition from any of the other five this adapter produces, which is why the class name and the sub-reason are both stated as expected values.

reference_behaviours.behaviour: partial parse as a first-class outcome
reference_behaviours.what_this_file_fixes: counts.parse_status is 'partial': every parsable record is emitted, the one rejected record is counted under its named class, and the artifact is neither abandoned nor suppressed.
reference_behaviours.why_it_belongs_here: AAP 0.5.4 makes partial parse a first-class outcome rather than a failure. An adapter that abandoned the artifact on its first defective record would emit zero rows, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan -- so the three surviving rows carry as much of the assertion as the rejection does.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, tools.gitleaks.path_base -- read as input, never assumed. Its record_path_field is 'File'.
resolution_context.path_base_value_note: The recorded base is the pinned scan root. Its absolute form is deliberately not reproduced here: no absolute path appears anywhere in this file, and these rows hold for whatever absolute root the adapter is given.
resolution_context.recorded_invocation_shape: Eighteen invocations, each handed exactly one root-relative directory, with the runner's working directory set to the scan root.
resolution_context.invocation_source: runner-metadata.json tools.gitleaks.invocation_form and working_directory, corroborated independently by harness/bin/run-gitleaks.sh: it cds to the scan root at line 47 and loops one directory per invocation at lines 50-63.
resolution_context.why_the_base_is_invocation_dependent: gitleaks dir takes exactly one path and reports relative to the process working directory when handed more, so the base is a property of the invocation rather than of the tool (AAP 0.5.4). Both shapes are real: the historical harness AAP 0.2.3 describes passed all eighteen scope directories to a single invocation, and this provisioning passes one per invocation.
resolution_context.invariance_across_the_two_shapes: Here the two shapes give the same base, because the runner's working directory is the scan root. Every path below therefore holds under either reading. That is a fact about this provisioning rather than a licence to skip reading the metadata, and no runner may be edited to make one shape true (AAP 0.3.2).
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_ALREADY_ROOT_RELATIVE -- the basis resolve_recorded_path records where the recorded base and the scan root are the same location, so the reported File was already root-relative and the join changed nothing.
resolution_context.path_kind_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, path_kind_for: no '!' separator and no leading '..' segment, so every emitted path names a location inside the scanned tree. Whether the file exists on disk is a separate question, and each of the three does exist at the pin -- recorded per row.
resolution_context.severity_source: None. The eighteen keys a pinned-Gitleaks record carries include no severity-like field, and this fixture carries no Severity key on any of its four elements, so every emitted row goes through severity.SeverityResult.absent().
resolution_context.severity_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py, BASIS_NO_VOCABULARY. absent() carries severity_native null, severity_norm Info and that basis, and its __post_init__ refuses a severity_native on it -- so the absence is structural rather than a convention a caller has to remember.
resolution_context.severity_selected_entry_note: null on this path: nothing was used to derive the band, so there is neither a label nor a score entry to record. No native literal is synthesised -- inventing one would put a literal into oss-scan-results/severity-map.md that the tool never emitted.
resolution_context.severity_map_consequence: The tally is fed once per emitted row, so three rows reach it and the rejected record reaches it not at all. severity-map.md can therefore name gitleaks as a tool that defines no severity vocabulary with a row count behind the statement, and no literal from the rejected record appears there.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A secret finding names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. AAP 0.5.4's unformable-coordinate rejection reaches dependency-oriented records only, so the absence here is not a rejection condition and this fixture's rejection has nothing to do with it.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve: null on every row. The shape carries no weakness or advisory identifier; deriving a CWE from a rule id would be inference of exactly the kind AAP 0.5.4 forbids.

single_identifier_route.statement: Gitleaks offers exactly one route to a finding's rule identifier -- the record's own RuleID -- so removing or emptying that key is both sufficient and complete as an expression of the missing-identifier condition. This is the simplest form of the condition in this folder.
single_identifier_route.authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py: _adapt_record reads the identifier once, through _text_field(record, 'RuleID'), and there is no second lookup anywhere in the module.
single_identifier_route.contrast_with_sarif: The SARIF adapter has two routes and a resolution step between them: a result's own ruleId, and an index into runs[].tool.driver.rules[] by ruleIndex where the ruleId is absent. Its missing-identifier fixture must therefore defeat both routes at once -- no ruleId and no usable ruleIndex -- and it additionally has an unusable-index case that has no counterpart here. That is why reject-sarif-missing-rule-id.sarif is the complicated form of this condition and this fixture is the simple one.
single_identifier_route.no_synthesis_permitted: No identifier may be synthesised from any other key. Description is the message source and nothing else; File is the path source; Tags is in NEVER_READ_FIELDS and is the empty array on all four elements in any case. A rule id assembled from any of them would be a value the tool never stated, which AAP 0.5.4's 'reject rather than infer' forbids -- and the rejection is precisely what keeps the record visible instead.
single_identifier_route.no_synthesis_is_checkable: Mechanically, not just by assertion: none of the three surviving rule_id values -- generic-api-key, github-pat, jwt -- occurs as a substring of its own record's Description or File, so a substring test over the surviving rows would catch an adapter that had derived an identifier from either.

empty_identifier_subtlety.statement: The one subtlety this condition still has is whether an identifier that is present but empty counts as present. It does not. That is why the empty-string variant earns a place beside the absent-key variant rather than being redundant with it.
empty_identifier_subtlety.why_a_loose_check_gets_it_wrong: A membership test ('RuleID' in record) or a not-None test reports the key as present for the empty string and lets the record through as a row whose rule_id is ''. emit.py then refuses it, because rule_id is in emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS and an empty required field would make the CSV round trip lossy -- an empty cell means null. So a loose check turns a record that should have been counted under a named class into either a raised write or, worse, a row asserting a rule that has no name.
empty_identifier_subtlety.how_the_adapter_gets_it_right: _text_field strips the value and treats an empty or all-whitespace result as the absence it is, returning the reason 'the record's RuleID is empty'. _text_reject_class then maps it to missing_rule_id rather than malformed_record, because the observed value is a string: an absence and an empty string are both the field's own missing class, while a non-string -- a list, an object, a number -- is a defect in the record's shape and is malformed_record instead.

empty_string.expected_outcome: one rejection under missing_rule_id, with the detail naming the value as empty

absent_key.expected_outcome: one rejection under the same class, missing_rule_id, with the detail naming the key as absent -- 'the record carries no RuleID, so the finding names no rule'. Both variants are the same class by design: _text_reject_class returns the field's missing class for a None and for a str alike, and the sub-reason is what distinguishes them. No element of this fixture exercises it, so this file asserts nothing about it; the statement is here because the condition's name covers both forms and a reader must not infer from its absence that the absent-key form would be classified differently.

all_whitespace_string.expected_outcome: the same rejection as the empty string, because _text_field strips before testing. Not exercised here either.

empty_identifier_subtlety.why_it_is_a_rejection_and_not_a_null_fie: rule_id is not among the five fields AAP 0.8.2 permits absent -- those are exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate, which emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS carries verbatim. A record with no usable identifier therefore has no valid row representation at all, so counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record nor invents an identifier for it.

attribution.statement: The rejection is attributable to the identifier alone. Element /1 is otherwise entirely well-formed: it is a JSON object, its Description is a non-empty rule description, its File is a real root-relative path in the pinned tree, and its StartLine is the integer 46, which is within that file's 71 lines.
attribution.control_evidence: Element /1 and element /2 were compared key by key and differ in exactly two of the eighteen: RuleID, which is the empty string against 'github-pat', and Fingerprint, which the adapter never reads (it is a declared member of NEVER_READ_FIELDS). Every other key is equal, File and StartLine and Description included. Element /2 becomes row 1 below. So the fixture contains its own control: the same record with a usable identifier is emitted, and the only difference between the two outcomes is the identifier.
attribution.no_other_condition_is_in_play: None of the adapter's other five rejection classes could claim this record. It is an object, so not malformed_record; its Description is non-empty, so not missing_message; its File is non-empty and resolves, so neither absent_path nor unresolvable_path; and its StartLine is a positive integer, so not non_integer_start_line.
attribution.later_steps_are_never_reached: The identifier is step 2 of the adapter's fixed five-step classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Rejecting at step 2 means this record's Description is never read as a message, its File is never resolved, its StartLine is never examined, its SymlinkFile is never tested for a second location, and no severity result is ever built for it. Several counter values below follow from that and are not miscounts: see counters_note.

rejection_boundary.statement: A missing rule identifier is a rejection. It is not a row with a null rule_id, not a row with a substituted identifier, and not a dropped record. The three alternatives each hide the record or assert something the tool did not state; counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: rule_id is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. emit.py refuses an empty or null required field rather than writing one, so there is no valid twelve-field row for a record with no usable identifier.

not_a_rejection.case: a rule identifier that is present, non-empty and unrecognised -- a rule name no ruleset this run pinned defines
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row carrying that identifier verbatim
not_a_rejection.evidence: The adapter validates the identifier's presence and type, never its membership in any rule list. Judging whether a rule exists or matters is outside this dataset (AAP 0.3.2), and the three surviving rows carry their identifiers exactly as the tool wrote them.

not_a_rejection.case: a record whose path resolves outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected (AAP 0.9.3). No element here resolves outside the globs, so rows_out_of_scope is 0; the declared-derived sibling expected/derived-gitleaks-features.rows.json covers that case with a lockfile outside the twelve roots.

not_a_rejection.case: a record with no StartLine at all
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with start_line null, counted under start_line_absent
not_a_rejection.evidence: start_line is one of the five fields absence is permitted for, so an absent line is a null field rather than a rejection. Only a StartLine that is present and unusable is the non_integer_start_line condition, which reject-gitleaks-non-integer-start-line.json owns.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_identifier: The rejected record is rejected and counted, never given an identifier. Nothing in this file supplies one for it, not even a plausible one, and nothing derives one from its Description, its File or its Tags.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of the top-level array -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction; its _count_gitleaks is the array's length and nothing else
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records('gitleaks', doc), which builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. Here it is len(array), so the left-hand side is 4 whatever the adapter does with the elements -- including the defective one, which the counting traversal counts exactly like the other three because it counts elements rather than findings it can read.
counts.every_element_yields_exactly_one_outcome: One row or one rejection per element, never both and never neither. _adapt_record returns a single value of one of the two types, so the property is structural rather than asserted. Three elements carry a non-empty RuleID and Description, a non-empty root-relative File and a StartLine that is an integer of at least 1, and become rows; the fourth is rejected at step 2.
counts.row_order: fixture order, preserved -- elements /0, /2 and /3 become rows 0, 1 and 2. Both output files use this order and emit.py compares them ordered row by row, so an expected file in any other order would assert something the pipeline does not promise. A rejected element consumes no row index: element /3 is row 2, not row 3.
counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = 'partial', assigned where there are rejections and 'clean' where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class with its sub-reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse -- the reconciliation assertion over this fixture passes, and the artifact's parse is partial, and both statements are true at once.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): six authored keys, then one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member -- fifteen keys in that order, which is the key set and the order above. Deliberately absent from it, and so from here: any adapter-side count of records walked, rows or rejections. Those are len(rows), len(rejections) and reconcile.count_records, and a plausible substitute published here is how the independent-traversal requirement would quietly be lost.
counters_note: Every counter here is keyed to three rather than four, and that is the classification order made visible rather than a miscount. The rejected element is rejected at step 2, before the multi-location test, before path resolution and before any severity result is built -- so it contributes to no path_kind_*, no severity_basis_*, neither in_scope counter, and not to multi_location_records either. severity_absent is 3 and severity_basis_no_vocabulary is 3 by policy rather than by observation: every emitted row of this tool takes that path. rows_in_scope plus rows_out_of_scope is 3 + 0 = 3, one measurement split rather than a second count of the same thing, and it equals counts.rows rather than counts.raw_finding_records -- a counter set that summed to 4 would mean the rejected record had produced a row.

counters_aap_0_5_4_reported.note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool. Two of them -- multi_location_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are keys of this adapter's own counter set and appear above with the same values. The other two are not: a Gitleaks record carries no CWE or CVE field at all, so no record can be multi-valued in either, and the adapter keys no counter it could never increment. They are stated here as 0 by construction so the four required numbers are all present in one place, and so that the difference between 'measured 0' and '0 because the field does not exist in this shape' is legible rather than inferred from a missing key. multi_location_records is 0 by measurement: SymlinkFile is the empty string on all four elements, so no record names a second location, and the rejected one would not have been tested for it anyway.
counters_aap_0_5_4_reported.non_filesystem_path_proportion: 0 of 3 emitted rows. run-record.md reports the count and the proportion for the dataset; for this fixture both are zero, because all three emitted paths name files inside the scanned tree.

redaction_invariant.requirement: AAP 0.5.4: Gitleaks runs with redaction so a matched secret's value never enters an artifact, and no adapter carries a secret value into any field. This file is committed to git -- .gitignore line 31 matches artifacts/ and nothing under oss-scan-results/ -- so the invariant has to hold of this file as written, not only of the dataset the adapter produces.
redaction_invariant.message_source_on_every_row: Description, the rule's own description. Never Secret, never Match, and never Message, which is a git commit message rather than a description. There is deliberately no fallback: every candidate would either infer content the tool did not state or carry a captured value into the field.
redaction_invariant.keys_never_read_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, NEVER_READ_FIELDS. Fingerprint is excluded even though this artifact's value is a file-rule-line composite: in commit mode it also carries a commit identity, and a field whose safety depends on which mode ran is not a field to read. That exclusion is what makes the defective element's altered Fingerprint irrelevant to its outcome.
redaction_invariant.keys_read_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, SOURCE_FIELDS -- the four keys a row is built from, named one at a time. The record is never copied, spread or iterated into a row, which is what makes the invariant structural there; here it is upheld by deriving each of the twelve values from those four keys and fixed constants alone.
redaction_invariant.symlink_file_is_the_one_exception: SymlinkFile is the single key outside SOURCE_FIELDS the adapter looks at, and only through a predicate returning a bool. It is a filesystem path rather than a captured value, it is never emitted, and it is never substituted for an absent File. It is the empty string on all four elements here, so it decides nothing beyond leaving multi_location_records at 0.
redaction_invariant.the_rejection_detail_is_also_covered: A rejection reason is the other channel a value could escape through, and it is closed the same way. _safe_value_repr renders only None, a bool, an int and a float, and names the type alone for anything else -- a str above all. The expected detail recorded under rejections below carries no value from the record: it names the key and says it is empty, which is the whole of what happened.
redaction_invariant.check_performed: Every distinct Match, Secret and Fingerprint value in the fixture -- five values across the four elements -- was tested as a substring against the whole of this file, prose included. Zero hits, which is the required result. Two drafting consequences follow: no sentence here quotes the placeholder string the runner's redaction flag substitutes for a captured value, and nowhere is a path, a rule id and a line number joined into one colon-separated string, since that is the shape of this artifact's fingerprint values.
redaction_invariant.upstream_protection_is_not_the_check: The runner passes a redaction flag, so a captured value never reached the artifact in the first place. That is upstream protection in a runner this run may not edit, and it is not a substitute for the assertion above, which is made against this file's own bytes.

prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: Trivy's adapter also reports secrets, and the SARIF adapter has its own missing-identifier fixture. Nothing here compares tools, ranks them, explains why one found something another did not, or folds one into the other (AAP 0.3.2). The one comparison this file does make -- against the SARIF adapter's two identifier routes, under single_identifier_route -- is about the shape of an artifact and the code that reads it, not about what either tool found or how well it found it.
prohibitions_observed.no_judging: No row is characterised as real, important, a false positive or a duplicate, and the rejected record is not called a false positive either: it is a record this pipeline cannot represent, which is a statement about the record's fields rather than about whether anything was really leaked.
prohibitions_observed.no_dedup: Elements /1 and /2 name the same file and the same line, and /1 and /2 share a Description. They are distinct records: one is rejected and one becomes a row, and neither is folded into the other. Two byte-identical elements would likewise be two outcomes.
prohibitions_observed.no_invented_severity: The tool defines no severity vocabulary, so none is invented: severity_native stays null on every row and severity_norm comes from the fixed no-vocabulary policy rather than from a guess at what a finding deserves. The rejected record gets no severity at all, not even Info.
prohibitions_observed.kept_not_filtered: No element is dropped. Three are emitted and one is counted, which together account for all four -- the arithmetic under counts is what makes the absence of filtering checkable rather than merely stated.
prohibitions_observed.never_derived_by_running_the_adapter: Every value in this file was read out of the fixture and the authored contracts: the field sources and the five-step classification order from adapters/gitleaks.py, the class name from paths.py, the band and basis from severity.py, the field set and its absence rules from emit.py, the count unit from reconcile.py, and the path base from runner-metadata.json. Nothing here was produced by invoking the adapter and recording its output, which would make the test a tautology.
prohibitions_observed.agreement_check_disclosed: After these values were derived and written, the adapter was invoked over this fixture once and its rows, rejections and counters compared to what is recorded here; agreement was complete, including the rejection class, the detail string and the record_identity mapping. That is disclosed in the same spirit as the corroboration below: it followed derivation, it could only ever have surfaced a disagreement to diagnose, and it contributed no value to this file.

corroboration.note: All three surviving rows have counterparts in the declared-derived sibling expected/derived-gitleaks-features.rows.json, because their fixture elements are byte-identical to elements of oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json: this file's row 0 is that file's row 1, row 1 is its row 3, and row 2 is its row 2. All thirty-six field comparisons agree. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.
corroboration.rejected_record_has_no_counterpart: The defective element appears in no captured artifact and in no other expected file, and it contributes no dataset row, so nothing corroborates it and nothing needs to: it is checkable by reading the fixture against adapters/gitleaks.py's classification order.
corroboration.dataset_counterpart: None of the three rows appears in oss-scan-results/findings.json. The committed dataset carries exactly one gitleaks row, for a file none of these elements names, so the dataset corroborates nothing here -- which is expected of a derived fixture and is stated rather than left as a gap a reader might read as a discrepancy.

rows.message: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Uncovered a GitHub Personal Access Token, potentially leading to unauthorized repository access and sensitive content exposure.
Uncovered a JSON Web Token, which may lead to unauthorized access to web applications and sensitive user data.

row_derivations.source: derived -- byte-identical to element /1 of oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json, compared field by field including key order
row_derivations.rule_id_route: the record's own RuleID, the only route this shape offers
row_derivations.severity_native_absent_reason: the record carries no severity-like field, and the tool defines no severity vocabulary
row_derivations.symlink_counterpart: absent -- SymlinkFile is the empty string, so the record names no second location and multi_location_records does not count it
row_derivations.absent_optional_fields_reason: the shape supplies no weakness identifier, no advisory identifier and no package coordinate; for a secret record the coordinate's absence is not a rejection condition
row_derivations.anchor_note: The same file and line the taint A/B subject file carries elsewhere in this run, and the same 380-line count expected/derived-gitleaks-features.rows.json records for it. start_line 241 is well inside the file.

row_derivations.source: derived -- byte-identical to element /3 of oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json, compared field by field including key order
row_derivations.rule_id_route: the record's own RuleID, the only route this shape offers
row_derivations.severity_native_absent_reason: the record carries no severity-like field, and the tool defines no severity vocabulary
row_derivations.symlink_counterpart: absent -- SymlinkFile is the empty string
row_derivations.anchor_note: This is the control for the rejected element: /1 is this record with its RuleID emptied, and the two differ in exactly two keys. Its path also demonstrates that the Kubernetes glob's mid-path ** reaches docker/src/main, a directory that is scanned by the file-based tools while being no Maven module.

row_derivations.source: derived -- byte-identical to element /2 of oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-gitleaks-features.json, compared field by field including key order
row_derivations.rule_id_route: the record's own RuleID, the only route this shape offers
row_derivations.severity_native_absent_reason: the record carries no severity-like field, and the tool defines no severity vocabulary
row_derivations.symlink_counterpart: absent -- SymlinkFile is the empty string
row_derivations.anchor_note: A Python test module, and in scope: it is one of the 832 test modules under python/pyspark/** that carry no src/test path segment, so the literal exclusion does not reach it and in_scope is true. Its test-ness is expressed as a tests/ directory and a test_ filename rather than as a Maven src/test tree. No test of any language is executed by this run -- the module is read by a scanner exactly as any other in-scope source is.
row_derivations.file_line_count_measurement: Measured at the pinned tree, whose HEAD was verified equal to the pinned SHA before measuring: 391 by wc -l, by counting newline bytes, and by len(bytes.splitlines()), the file ending in a newline. expected/derived-gitleaks-features.rows.json records 391 for the same file independently.
row_derivations.file_line_count_divergence_disclosed: This file's own specification stated 384 lines for this path. The measured value is 391 and that is what is recorded, for two reasons: an expected file must carry measured values rather than asserted ones, and a count appearing in two documents must be one measurement cited twice rather than two measurements -- 384 here would contradict expected/derived-gitleaks-features.rows.json. No field of row 2 changes either way, because start_line 167 is inside the file under both readings, so this is a disclosed divergence in a stated line count and not a difference in any expected value.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and record_index name the same element. The index is carried as well because the adapter passes exactly record_index into the rejection it builds, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation can be compared directly, without translating one coordinate system into the other. The array index is the locator for this shape: a bare array of findings offers no rule pointer, no run index and no section to name.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_MISSING_RULE_ID constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.reject_class_is_declared_producible: The class is a member of adapters/gitleaks.py's REJECT_CLASSES_PRODUCED, which declares the six conditions this adapter can produce rather than leaving them to be discovered by reading the code.
rejections.classification_step: step 2 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Step 1 passes: the element is a JSON object. Steps 3, 4 and 5 are never reached.
rejections.why_not_malformed_record: _text_reject_class returns the field's own missing class for a value that is absent or is a string, and malformed_record only for a value that is present and is not a string. The observed value is a string, so the class is missing_rule_id. A list, an object or a number in that key would have been malformed_record instead -- reject-gitleaks-malformed-record.json owns that case.
rejections.later_steps_never_examined: The record's Description, File, StartLine and SymlinkFile are never read, so no interaction with any other rejection condition is in play. Worth stating because the fixture gives the defective record a perfectly good value for each of them, and a reader could otherwise expect one of them to matter.
rejections.expected_detail: the record's RuleID is empty, so the finding names no rule
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted here because a class name alone would not distinguish an empty identifier from an absent one -- both are missing_rule_id. It is composed by the adapter as the field reason followed by ', so the finding names no rule'. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings rather than by full-string equality.
rejections.expected_detail_carries_no_record_value: The detail names the key and its emptiness. It renders no value from the record: _safe_value_repr admits only None, a bool, an int and a float, and this failure path does not render the observed value at all.
rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies record_index and nothing else on this path -- deliberately not rule_id, which is the very thing the record does not have. Later steps add rule_id to a rejection's identity because by then one exists; a path rejection from paths.resolve_gitleaks_path carries RuleID, StartLine and File instead. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no identifier to put in the row. rule_id is never absent from a row, so a record with no usable identifier has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or synthesising an identifier from its Description, its File or its Tags -- would each either hide it or assert something the tool never stated. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so no entry from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none -- which for this tool means the three emitted rows are the whole of its contribution to the no-vocabulary count.
rejections.contributes_no_counter: It increments none of the fifteen counters. Every counter this adapter keys is incremented at step 3 or later, so a step-2 rejection touches none of them.
rejections.not_produced_by_another_fixture: The other four reject-gitleaks-* fixtures own the other conditions -- malformed-record, missing-message, non-integer-start-line and unresolvable-path, the last carrying an element whose File is the empty string, which is the absent_path class. This fixture re-covers none of them, and each of them still has its own work to do.

in_scope_verification.method: Each of the three emitted paths was matched against the twelve globs by hand and then checked twice more, with two implementations that are not the one under test: a glob-to-regex translation written for this check, and CPython 3.13's PurePosixPath.full_match, whose ** spans zero or more directories. All three agree on all three paths.
in_scope_verification.why_not_fnmatch: Three of the twelve globs depend on ** matching zero or more directories, and neither fnmatch nor PurePath.match provides those semantics. A matcher built on either silently drops whole modules, and a silently dropped module looks exactly like a module with nothing to report (AAP 0.5.4).
in_scope_verification.src_test_rule: The exclusion is the literal substring src/test. No path here contains it, including the Python test module.
in_scope_verification.the_rejected_record_has_no_in_scope_valu: in_scope is a field of a row, and the rejected record produces none. Its File would have matched the Kubernetes glob had it been evaluated -- element /2 proves that, being the same path -- but it was never evaluated, and recording an in_scope value for a record that produced no row would assert a field the dataset does not contain.
in_scope_verification.result: three in scope, none out of scope
